$comment: FP-6501 fire pump twin. Expected values in Maximo Monitor from the listed pump curve, NFPA 20 / NFPA 25 rules and the controller settings; the controller and the test rig send only what they measure.

identification.model: 8100 Series 8x6x18F horizontal split-case fire pump, curve A-8853, 16 in impeller
identification.description: Electric fire pump of the sprinkler and standpipe system of a distribution warehouse (one pump, city water supply)
identification.driver: 125 hp, 1780 rpm, 460 V 3-phase induction motor (open drip-proof), flexible coupling
identification.controller: Listed electric fire pump controller, across-the-line start, pressure transducer and event log
identification.jockey: Vertical multistage jockey (pressure maintenance) pump with its own controller
identification.listing: UL listed and FM approved for 1000 gpm at 72-122 psi (8x6x18F casing, per curve A-8853)
identification.pump: Horizontal split-case, single stage, 8x6 casing (8 in suction, 6 in discharge), 6-vane impeller trimmed to 16 in (the trim is an assumption: replace with your pump's nameplate)

pump.source: A-C Fire Pump curve A-8853 (8x6x18F, 8100 Series, 1780 rpm, 1000 GPM), 16 in impeller (curve B): points read from the published curve image, about +/- 1.5 psi / +/- 2 hp. Replace with the certified shop test curve of your pump. Rated pressure = the curve at 1000 gpm; the fit is a cubic in thousands of gpm (largest residual 0.20 psi). The curve is total head in psi; the twin uses it as net pressure (discharge - suction), as NFPA 25 test sheets do, and neglects the velocity pressure difference between the 8 in and 6 in flanges.

nfpa20.source: NFPA 20 (Installation of Stationary Pumps for Fire Protection): shut-off head not above 140 % of rated head; 150 % of rated capacity at not less than 65 % of rated head.

nfpa25.source: NFPA 25 (Inspection, Testing and Maintenance of Water-Based Fire Protection Systems): annual flow test at churn, 100 % and 150 %; speed-corrected net pressure at least 95 % of the reference curve; electric no-flow test of at least 10 min. NFPA 25 allows a MONTHLY no-flow test for most electric pumps; this site keeps a weekly test (site programme, the twin's interval).

motor.source: assumption: typical value, replace with the motor nameplate. 125 hp is chosen above the 16 in curve's largest power (about 112 bhp); full-load current, efficiency and power factor are typical of a 125 hp 460 V 4-pole motor.

settings.source: NFPA 20 annex method: jockey stop = churn (curve at 0 gpm) + minimum static suction; jockey start 10 psi below the stop; fire pump start 5 psi below the jockey start. Minimum and nominal static suction of the city main, normal time to run of an across-the-line start and the jockey pump flow: assumption: typical value, replace with the water authority's flow test, the controller's commissioning record and the jockey pump data sheet.

supply.source: Suction pressure at 150 % flow during the acceptance test, and the minimum the water authority allows at the suction flange: assumption: typical value, replace with your water authority's limit. NFPA 20 is commonly quoted as allowing the suction pressure to fall to 0 psi at 150 % flow; many authorities ask for 20 psi.

demo.note: Demo only: the controller runs a no-flow (churn) test every 60 s of real time instead of every week, and the stored annual flow test follows the injected fault directly, as if the test were repeated.

points.label: Discharge pressure (= system pressure at standby)
Flow through the test meter (0 at churn and standby)
System pressure at the last automatic start
Last start: start signal to motor running
Automatic starts on low pressure, not tests, last 30 days
Jockey pump running time, last 24 h
Net pressure at the end of the last churn test
Speed during the last churn test
Packing gland temperature at the end of the last churn test
Days since the last churn test
Days since the last annual flow test

twin_model.source: 95 % (NFPA 25) and 65 % (NFPA 20) are from the standards. Room 4.4 °C (40 °F) is the pump-room minimum commonly applied for electric pumps in NFPA 25 weekly inspections. Every other limit: assumption: typical value, replace with your own maintenance strategy.

failure_modes.$comment: Each failure mode: what degrades, how it shows, the rules that see it.

impeller_wear.name: Impeller and wear-ring wear
impeller_wear.symptoms: churn pressure a few % low; annual test points fall below 95 % of the curve, most at 150 %

weak_supply.name: Weak water supply or partly closed suction valve
weak_supply.symptoms: static suction low; suction at 150 % flow below the authority minimum

system_leak.name: Leak in the sprinkler system
system_leak.symptoms: jockey pump starts many times a day; make-up flow above 1 gpm

jockey_failed.name: Jockey pump failed
jockey_failed.symptoms: no jockey starts, system pressure below the jockey start; the fire pump starts on its own

pressure_sensing_drift.name: Controller pressure transducer drift
pressure_sensing_drift.symptoms: the fire pump starts far from its set pressure

starter_fault.name: Starter or contactor fault
starter_fault.symptoms: time from start signal to running grows

packing_overtight.name: Packing overtightened or dry
packing_overtight.symptoms: no drip at the glands, packing hot at the end of the churn test

tests_skipped.name: Churn and flow tests skipped
tests_skipped.symptoms: days since the last churn test and the last flow test grow
